frontmatter.claim: A break of a multi-week Donchian range persists because risk is repriced slowly: systematic participants scale in over days and trapped counter-positions cover into the move, so the tail of a breakout is fatter than its body. A trailing stop harvests that tail, while a fixed target amputates it and turns a positive-expectancy mechanism into a losing one. Long: close > donchian_hi(100); short: close < donchian_lo(100); stop: ATR 2.0; target: none; trail: arm at 1R, ATR 4.0; max 500 bars.
Buying shallow pullbacks within an aligned EMA stack captures short-term trend continuation at reduced risk, based on anchoring and delayed discretionary entry.
A trend-persistence strategy that enters on shallow pullbacks within aligned EMA stacks, using adx_min=28 and pullback_atr=0.5 as gene parameters.
A trend-following strategy using ADX minimum 28.0, pullback ATR 1.2, and 15-minute timeframe, designed for unstable trends with strict confirmation and conservative pullback entries.

An ema_trend variant using adx_min=26.8812, pullback_atr=0.8, and trend_tf=15m was retired after 8 closed trades (8 wins, +46.33 USDT), suggesting the parameter set was not retained despite a perfect win record.

In leveraged crypto perp trends, entering on EMA(50) pullbacks in the direction of EMA(50)/EMA(200) alignment, filtered by OI expansion (oi_ret(24) > 0.02), non-extreme funding (|funding_z(96)| < 1.5), relative volume > 1.0, and ADX(14) > 20, with ATR stop (2.5x), ATR trail armed at 1R (3.0x), and 200-bar time stop, captures reflexive positioning-driven continuation.

A long strategy that enters when price makes a new 192-bar Donchian high while 1920-bar funding z-score is below zero, filtered by ADX(14) > 18, with ATR(2.5) stop, 3.0 RR target, no trail, and max 64 bars. The thesis is that new highs with cooling funding indicate a non-leveraged, healthier rally that tends to persist.

frontmatter.claim: A strong BTC impulse can be followed by delayed capital rotation into ETH, large caps and then smaller alts.
High trading effort with little price progress can indicate absorption or exhaustion.
Extremely one-sided funding can indicate crowded positioning and increased vulnerability to a squeeze or reversal.
Price can move beyond an obvious swing to trigger resting stops and collect liquidity before the subsequent directional move.
A persistent imbalance between bid and ask liquidity can indicate asymmetric short-term pressure, but it is unreliable when displayed liquidity is unstable or deceptive.
Extreme momentum readings inside an established trend can indicate that continuation is becoming crowded or exhausted.
Anchoring, under-reaction and herding can cause price trends to persist over short horizons.
In non-trending regimes, sufficiently large deviations from anchored VWAP can revert as temporary overreaction is absorbed by liquidity providers.

In RANGING regimes, when price makes an extreme low/high but RSI momentum over the same 96-bar window refuses to confirm, passive/lagging flow is absorbing the last move; entering on this divergence with an ATR stop (2.5x), trailing exit armed at 1R (3x ATR), ADX<25 and rel_volume>1.0 filters, and max 200 bars aims to capture a snap fueled by late trend chasers.
